activity_context.topic_title: The Rank-Nullity Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Rank or Nullity of a Linear Transformation Using the Rank-Nullity Theorem
examples.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3.$ If $\textrm{nullity}(\mathbf{T})=1,$ then what is $\textrm{rank}(\mathbf{T})?$
examples.worked_solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n,$ then

$$
\textrm{rank}(\mathbf{T}) + \textrm{nullity}(\mathbf{T}) = n.
$$

For the given transformation, we have $n=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T) & =n \\ \text{rank}(T)+1 & =3 \\ \text{rank}(T) & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
